### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in probeOrganizationMember))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in probeOrganizationMember))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in probeOrganizationMember))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 40 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `28c03049ab68f9abb90f5901970874b4f0ab4fa6` — the merge of head `41de6f56d8797f55610ae48e799270eac4891c84` into base `e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 28c03049ab68f9abb90f5901970874b4f0ab4fa6 && git checkout 28c03049ab68f9abb90f5901970874b4f0ab4fa6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620 41de6f56d8797f55610ae48e799270eac4891c84 && git checkout -B drift-repro e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620 && git merge --no-ff 41de6f56d8797f55610ae48e799270eac4891c84

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3c36f9c6edfb7f70ef9143b0e65bc1fb036d49d8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/runtime/src/seed-org-scoped-references.integration.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/system-names.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-field.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts

Inputs read: cards #33207 and #33206 (bodies and all five comments each, the claim amendments 6871524022 and 6871533047 included), PR #33222 (body, four files, net diff against `main`), and the 53 check-runs on this head: every run that executed concluded success (Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, TypeScript Type Check, Lint and Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Build Docs, Spec property liveness); the rest are path-filtered skips. No earlier contract-review record exists on either card or the PR.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: no exported symbol, schema key or config field is added, removed or re-shaped. `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` is untouched (packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts:735); the new members are module-private (`carriesOrganizationColumn`, `ProbeRefusal`, `DatabaseProbeOutcome`) or private class members. `Metadata-protocol: none` is RIGHT.
- Accept-set of the reference probe on a load pinned to an organization (seed-loader.ts:2797, 2898-2915): a `sys_user` target moves from never-resolves to resolves-through-`sys_member`; `sys_organization` from never to own-organization only; an author object with no `organization_id` column from never to unscoped; every other target is unchanged. The direction (widening) is RIGHT for the first two. The third is WRONG at its edge: see ④ finding 2.
- The key choice `tenantId` over the card's `organizationId` is RIGHT: a hook's `session.organizationId` is built from `execCtx.tenantId` (packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts:68) and `ExecutionContext` declares no `organizationId` key (execution-context.zod.ts:157). `{ isSystem: true, tenantId }` is also the shape the engine itself asks a system write to reach (packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts:337).
- The organization on the context is `config.organizationId ?? this.fallbackOrgId` (seed-loader.ts:1110), the same expression the stamp (1819) and the landed-key ledger (4259) use, so the write context, the stamp and the ledger cannot disagree. RIGHT. Each caller builds a fresh `SeedLoaderService` per load (packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:2054, 2157, 2585; packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts:105; packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:4980), and `seedOptions` is assigned on every `loadDatasets` before any write, so no stale bag reaches a write.
- The derived claim "the narrowing is a hook's `ctx.api` read" is INCOMPLETE: the same `tenantId` scopes the loader's own by-id updates and every engine-internal read that inherits the write context. See ④ finding 3.
- Probes still run under `{ isSystem: true }` with no `tenantId` (seed-loader.ts:2825, 2863, 2872), so the loader's own reads are not narrowed by the new context. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch` with the `!` subject and a BREAKING banner matches the repo rule (AGENTS.md:1027-1028: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition). `@objectstack/runtime` only re-exports the class (packages/runtime/src/seed-loader.ts) and its one changed file is a test, so one package is the right set. The ADR-0087 marker is present and its category (no migration prescription) fits: no key or stored row changes shape. Check Changeset is green on this head.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right arm, and it is present line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset.
- The line's content is not accurate to the diff in three places, each tied to a ④ finding: (a) "a reference to a person resolves to a person who is a member of that organization" holds only while the member is among at most 50 unordered same-key matches (finding 1); (b) "an object its author declared global (`tenancy: { enabled: false }`, no `organization_id` column)" is narrower than the code's rule, which is "no `organization_id` column and no `managedBy`" (finding 2); (c) the narrowed member names only a hook's `ctx.api` read, and "nothing that resolved before stops resolving" does not hold for the row class in finding 3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` is empty on both dev reports; nothing to escalate from it.
- Dev flag "AppPlugin's no-metadata basic-insert fallback writes with `SEED_WRITE_OPTIONS` and no organization": answered, accepted. It stamps nothing and carries no organization, so there is nothing for a hook to be told; it is outside both cards.
- Dev flag "platform-managed tables with no organization column other than `sys_user` and `sys_organization` keep a refused probe": answered, accepted. Keeping the refusal and reporting it (seed-loader.ts:2839, 2924) is the conservative arm; no scope rule is invented.
- Dev note "`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally": answered by the head's Lint and Repo Gates run, success.
- Dev note on the local dogfood red file (TS7016 from a declaration-less rebuild): answered by the head's Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and Dogfood Regression Gate, all success; it does not reach the diff.
- The brief's own instruction to post this record is superseded by the dispatching instruction for this round: the record is written to the scratch path only and posted nowhere by this seat.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself holds against the published spec: it does not take a declared capability away at the consumer. `main` never declared that a system write on behalf of one organization reads every organization's rows; the walled read scope for a context that carries an organization is the engine's own published rule (packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, the `organization` and `deny` rungs; packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts:424-445), and the seed context simply had no organization to be scoped by. Giving it the organization the rows are stamped with makes that rule real for seed writes, and `ctx.api.sudo()` remains the declared way out. Under `single` nothing narrows (the verdict is `none` for a system context). The membership rule for `sys_user`, the own-organization rule for `sys_organization` and the narrowed catch are sound in shape. The three findings below are in how the diff delivers it.

1. **must-fix** — the membership probe is driven from the wrong side, so the declared capability is not delivered at hosted scale, and it then misreports why. packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts:2859-2877 reads up to `MEMBER_PROBE_CANDIDATES = 50` (3359) `sys_user` rows matching the natural key, with no ordering and no organization, and only then asks `sys_member` which of those 50 belong to the load's organization. The comment at 3355-3357 assumes the key "is meant to be unique", but identity lives above the organization: `name` is not unique in `sys_user`, and the card's own scenario is a hosted app whose sample people are provisioned under the same seeded names in each organization (#33207 body: `owner_id: 'Zhang Wei (Rep)'`, "after signing up the demo people under the seeded names"). Once a deployment holds more than 50 users with that name, the load organization's member falls outside an arbitrary 50-row window, the reference stays NULL, and line 2877 returns `nonMemberMatched: true`, so the pass-2 error (3226, 3252) states that the person "is not a member of organization X" when the person is. The failure is in the safe direction (nobody is borrowed) but the changeset's widened member is declared without this bound, and the result depends on driver row order. Fix shape: bound the probe by the organization, which is the small side (the load organization's `sys_member.user_id` set, then `sys_user` by key within that set, paged if needed), or page the candidates to exhaustion; in either case never say "not a member" on a truncated read. The test file pins two same-named people, not the cap (seed-org-scoped-references.integration.test.ts:203-217).

2. **should-fix** — the `global` rule keys on the wrong fact and opens a cross-organization borrow for a published object shape. `probeScopeOf` answers `global` for any target with no `organization_id` column and no `managedBy` (seed-loader.ts:2909-2912, via `carriesOrganizationColumn` at 516-523), and a `global` target is probed with no organization predicate under `{ isSystem: true }` (2816-2825). But "no `organization_id` column" is not "walled by nothing": the spec publishes `tenancy: { enabled: true, tenantField: 'workspace_id' }` for an object whose tenant column is not `organization_id` (packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:766-770, 783), and the wall resolves that column (packages/core/src/security/tenant-field.ts:65-80; packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts:246-257). Such an object that also sets `systemFields: { tenant: false }` (object.zod.ts:3665) carries no `organization_id`, is still walled per organization, and is now classified `global`: an organization's load resolves a natural key to the first match in ANY organization and writes that id as the link. On `main` the same probe was refused, so the reference stayed empty; the diff turns a safe miss into the cross-organization link the surrounding comment says is never made (2808-2811). The docs and the changeset describe the rule as `tenancy: { enabled: false }`; the code is broader than both. Fix shape: classify `global` only when the object resolves no tenant field at all (the reading `resolveTenantFieldName` already gives), and scope by the resolved field otherwise or keep the reported refusal. No pin covers it: the one global-target case uses a tenancy-disabled catalog (test file:235-239).

3. **should-fix** — the write context narrows more than the declared member, including the loader's own pass-2 write, where a miss is silent. Under a walled posture a system context that carries `tenantId` gets the driver scope `organization_id = tenantId` on every by-id update and its readback (engine-driver-options.ts:424-445 with no recorded verdict for a system context; packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts:1116; packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts:299-302, 324-326; sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts:102-130). On `main` the same update carried no organization and was unscoped. The loader states that "a record that supplies its own `organization_id` always wins" (seed-loader.ts:1814-1816, 1876-1877); such a row whose organization differs from the pinned one is still inserted, but its deferred back-fill (3283-3286) now matches zero rows, the driver returns `null`, `writeDeferredReference` discards the result, and the reference is counted as resolved while the column stays NULL. That is a link that was written before and is silently not written now, against the changeset's "nothing that resolved before stops resolving". The same scope also reaches every engine-internal read that inherits the context (for example `referenceCheckContext`, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts:348-350, which keeps the tenant scope by design), so roll-ups, parent reads and reference checks on a seeded row now read within the load organization. That behaviour is the consistent one and is what an API write by a member does, but the Clause-② line names only "a hook's `ctx.api` read". Fix shape: either refuse, or report as an error, a pass-2 update that lands on no row (so the miss is never silent), and widen the Clause-② narrowed member in the changeset and PR body to "every read and by-id write the seed write performs or triggers".

4. **nit** — a refusal raised by the `sys_member` half of the membership probe is reported as a refusal on `sys_user.FIELD` (seed-loader.ts:2839): the object and field named are not the ones the database refused. The code and the logged first sentence still identify it.

5. **nit** — the changeset and the PR body claim the narrowing for `isolated` or `group`; only `isolated` is pinned (test file:305-319). By reading, `group` projects the same single-organization scope for a context with no membership set (engine-driver-options.ts:440-443), so the claim holds by the cited code, without a pin.

6. **nit** — the `sys_user` branch asks membership even when the authored value went through the `id` probe leg, which is right, but a value `looksLikeInternalId` recognises is kept without any probe (pre-existing, outside the diff), so an authored UUID for a non-member is not judged by the new rule. Noted for a follow-up card; not a defect of this diff.

Finding 1 is a must-fix, so the round fails; findings 1 to 3 each earn a delta review of their fix on the new head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `752448bfb257be4ae4e3a5dac0e4cd5aa63ac3ac`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-deferred-failure.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/seed-org-scoped-references.integration.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-field.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts

Delta review of round 1 (FAIL on `3c36f9c6edfb7f70ef9143b0e65bc1fb036d49d8`): the two commits `bb0a4731a` and `752448bfb`, read as `git diff 3c36f9c6..752448bf` (five files, 282 insertions, 52 deletions), plus the updated PR body. Check-runs on this head at record time: concluded success are Check Changeset (one of its two runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint scoped tooling self-tests, Test UI, filter, Auto Label. NOT concluded (in progress): Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, all four Type Check jobs, Lint ESLint, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint docs and code guards, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint scoped query-options erasure, Lint scoped slot lookup and corpus, Live E2E UI, and the second Check Changeset run. No run has failed. This record judges the contract and the tree; it does not stand in for the gates that had not concluded, and the verdict below is void if any of them concludes red.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: still none added, removed or re-shaped. The delta adds one import of an existing export (`resolveTenantFieldName` from `@objectstack/core`, seed-loader.ts:37), private members (`writeOrganization`, `rowWriteOptions`, `writeOptionsFor`, `MEMBER_PROBE_PAGE`) and one optional field on the module-private `DeferredUpdate` (4726-4732). `Metadata-protocol: none` stays RIGHT.
- New derived behaviour, named RIGHT in the prose: a row that supplies its own `organization_id` different from the load's is written with `tenantId` set to its own organization (`writeOptionsFor`, 3424-3440), on the sequential write (3559), the batched insert (2515-2518, the batch flushing when the write organization changes, the flush binding its bag synchronously at 1567), the update of an existing row (2493-2494) and the pass-2 back-fill (3327, from `rowOrganization` annotated at 2550). This is consistent with the declared member "a hook sees the organization the row is stamped with" and removes the split between the row's stamp and its write context that round 1 finding 3 rested on. The row's own organization winning is a rule `main` already had (1822-1824); the delta makes the context follow it, it does not create a new cross-organization write.
- New error code `SEED_BACKFILL_NO_ROW` (3332-3340) is carried on a thrown error that the existing pass-2 catch reports and counts (3116 onward); it is a log and result-message detail, not a declared surface. RIGHT.
- The membership probe's answer is now deterministic (lowest id among members, 2889) where it was driver row order. RIGHT, and stated in the changeset.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and still right: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, `!` subject, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 marker; one concluded Check Changeset run is success on this head.
- The `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line now names the wider narrowed member in both the changeset and the PR body ("every read and by-id write a seed write performs or triggers ... scoped to the organization the row is written as"), the global member is restated as "an object no organization walls (no `organization_id` column and no tenant field)", and the person member is qualified by the paged read. Each of the three inaccuracies recorded in round 1 section ② is corrected. Accurate to the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round 1 nit 6 (an authored value `looksLikeInternalId` recognises skips the probe, so the membership rule never judges it) is left by the dev as follow-up material: accepted as a deviation; it is pre-existing and outside the diff. It should be carried by a card, which this seat does not file.
- The dev's question on fix shape for finding 1 (page the candidates versus drive from the member set) is answered in ④ item 1: the chosen shape closes the finding; its cost reasoning does not hold for the hosted case and is graded there.
- The dev's question on offset paging under a concurrent writer is answered in ④ item 5.
- The dev's measurement that real ObjectQL throws not-found on a by-id update its scope cannot see corrects the downstream half of round 1 finding 3: this seat traced the scoped update to the SQL driver's zero-row `null` and did not trace the engine's own refusal above it. The scoping itself, and the row class it broke, were as recorded; the outcome on the real stack was a loud failed back-fill, not a silent one. The new integration pin (test file, "a pass-2 back-fill the write organization cannot see") and the stub-engine unit pin cover both layers.

### ④ Design judgment

Round 1 findings, each judged on this head:

1. Round 1 must-fix (membership probe truncated at 50 unordered candidates, false "not a member"): CLOSED. `probeOrganizationMember` reads candidates with `orderBy id asc`, `limit 50`, increasing `offset` (seed-loader.ts:2884-2893; the keys are the engine contract's own, packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts:145, 151), asks `sys_member` per page, returns the first member, and returns `nonMemberMatched` only after an empty or short page (2895, 2913). The loop terminates on every path. Pinned by sixty same-named people with the member last in id order and a second organization that owns none of them (test file, "a member among more same-named people than one read holds").

2. Round 1 should-fix (`global` keyed on "no `organization_id` column"): CLOSED. `global` now also requires `resolveTenantFieldName(definition) === null` (2953), the reading the wall itself scopes by (packages/core/src/security/tenant-field.ts:65-80). An object walled by `tenancy.tenantField` keeps the organization-filtered probe, which is refused and reported; nothing is borrowed. Pinned with a `workspace_id`-walled object holding another organization's same-named row. Docs and changeset now state the rule the code has.

3.
